purpose: Phase C2 recall-gap analysis: for each oracle query, which browser-equivalent (exact cosine, C1.2 ground truth) candidates are completely absent from live Vectorize returnValues:true topK=30-per-namespace results -- not a ranking/ordering question, a presence/absence question.
method_note: Only the missing-from-server direction is meaningful here. The reverse (extra candidates present in server but not in the browser-equivalent list) is NOT reported as a finding -- it is largely an artifact of comparison-depth asymmetry (server queried topK=30/namespace; the browser-equivalent baseline was reconstructed from C1.2, which only saved each namespace's top10). A genuinely missing id, by contrast, cannot be explained by that asymmetry: server's window (30) was 3x WIDER than what browser-equivalent was checked against (10), so if server had full recall, all of browser's top10-per-namespace candidates should trivially reappear.

verification_chain: 1. C1.2 exact local sweep (registry/generated/*.f32.bin, zero Vectorize) ranks this chunk #1 for this query, cosine=0.515285, calibrated=0.1274
2. Phase C2 live Vectorize query (topK=30, returnValues:true, chunk namespace) does not return it
3. Direct probe: re-queried Vectorize with topK=50 (the max) -- still absent
4. Direct probe: fetched lm-002542#chunk-0..3 from Vectorize via get_by_ids -- vectors genuinely exist, 512-dim, real values (rules out a missing-upload explanation)
5. Recomputed cosine locally from the JUST-FETCHED Vectorize values (not reusing any earlier script/data) -- 0.515285, matches step 1 exactly
